basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 5-7.' and it opens 'VERS. 5-7.-- Et factum est omne tempus quod vixit Adam, nongenti triginta anni, et'. The printing's caput is stale here, its marker for this chapter being missing, so the chapter is taken from the lemma, whose best match anywhere in Genesis falls on the very verse the printing numbers.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 5-7.-- Et factum est omne tempus quod vixit Adam, nongenti triginta anni, et mortuus est. Juxta tropologiam, ut nonnulli interpretantur, anni Adae nongenti triginta, tres leges, vel fidem, spem et charitatem, vel tempus aetatis Christi significant.
